title: Multi-registry signed publish pipeline with automated rollback and SDK example updates
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Design and implement a single CI workflow that builds and publishes Python, TypeScript, and Go SDK artifacts to their respective registries (PyPI, npm, and Go module proxy). The pipeline must produce verifiable provenance metadata (checksums, SBOM, in-toto style attestations), sign release artifacts using a KMS-backed key (with a fallback HSM attestation flow), and support safe canary publishes plus automated rollback if post-publish checks fail.

Scope and goals:
- Produce wheel/sdist, npm tarballs, and go module zip + .info files with deterministic builds and embedded build metadata.
- Generate SBOM (CycloneDX) and per-artifact SHA256 checksums.
- Emit an in-toto-style provenance bundle signed by KMS and store the attestations in the release bucket.
- Integrate signing into the existing GitHub Actions release matrix and add a GitHub Action to verify KMS signature before publishing.
- Add a multi-registry publish step that can push to staging registries first, run smoke checks, then push to public registries.
- Implement an automated rollback path that revokes signatures and marks the release as deprecated in our internal index if post-publish regression checks fail.
- Update SDKs to surface an "X-SDK-Artifact-Hash" header on streaming requests and include example code demonstrating retry/backoff semantics and streaming ergonomics that align with the new artifact metadata.
- Provide example CI configs and local dev scripts for reproducing signed builds and verifying provenance.

Out of scope:
- Full redesign of the release dashboard UI (we will add links to CI artifacts and attestations to the existing release pages).

Acceptance criteria:
- Green pipeline that builds artifacts for python/typescript/go and uploads to staging registries.
- Each published artifact has a checksum file, SBOM, and a signed provenance attestation stored alongside the artifact.
- Canary publish path with automated smoke tests implemented; failing smoke tests trigger a documented rollback workflow that is automated where possible.
- SDK examples updated: python/ts/go examples in repo show how to verify artifact hash and how to use retry + streaming helpers.
- Documentation and runbook for release engineers and on-call describing how to investigate failed publish and perform manual rollback if automation cannot.
